name: Core Scientific

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Core Scientific logo.svg; Wikipedia infobox logo)

description: Core Scientific runs large power-heavy data centers in seven US states and is converting them from bitcoin mining into leased AI colocation space. In the first half of 2026 77% of revenue came from one customer, CoreWeave, which licenses powered data-hall space on 12-year terms and pays a fixed fee per megawatt once capacity is delivered, plus power costs passed through at cost. About 590 MW is leased to CoreWeave of which 395 MW was billing on 2026-06-30. The rest of the revenue is still the old business: mining bitcoin for its own account, which now loses money, and hosting one remaining customer's miners until the end of 2026. On 2026-07-27 it signed 15-year leases for 377 MW with AMD and 152 MW with a neocloud, with AMD also holding the right to lease up to 1,925 MW more through 2028. Net losses of $1.2 billion in Q2 2026 came mostly from a non-cash revaluation of warrants, not from operations. It restated 2024 and 2025 financials in March 2026 over an accounting error and has a material weakness in internal controls.

hq.note: Principal executive office listed on filings is 838 Walker Road, Suite 21-2105, Dover, DE 19904 (FY2025 10-K); Wikipedia describes Dover as the registered office and Austin, Texas as the operational headquarters

employees.note: 325 full-time employees in 26 US states (FY2025 10-K Item 1)

businessLines.name: Colocation (high-density colocation for AI and HPC)
businessLines.how: CoreWeave pays a fixed monthly license fee per megawatt of critical IT load under 10-plus-year agreements (12-year initial terms), starting when each block of capacity is delivered and becomes billable. Power cost is passed through to the customer with no markup and is shown gross in both revenue and cost, so it adds revenue but no profit. CoreWeave also prepays for capacity not yet delivered. The per-MW fee is not disclosed.
businessLines.description: Powered, cooled and secured data-hall space for CoreWeave (the sole colocation customer to date) at sites in Texas, Georgia, North Carolina, Kentucky, North Dakota, Alabama and Oklahoma.
businessLines.revenueNote: License fees $158,008K, power fees passed through $56,132K, maintenance and other $68K. Q2 2026 alone: $136,669K. FY2025: $65,424K (20% of revenue).

businessLines.name: Digital Asset Self-Mining
businessLines.how: Earns bitcoin as a member of a mining pool in return for computing power, so revenue moves with the bitcoin price and network difficulty. Electricity is the main cost and is not passed to anyone, so margins are negative at current prices.
businessLines.description: Mining bitcoin for its own account at two remaining facilities; being wound down as power is reallocated to colocation.
businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2025 was $129,603K; bitcoin mined fell 49% and average bitcoin price fell 23%. FY2025: $229,207K (72% of revenue).

businessLines.name: Digital Asset Hosted Mining
businessLines.how: The customer owns the mining machines; Core Scientific supplies power, space, deployment, monitoring and repair and charges for power plus a service fee.
businessLines.description: Hosting a third party's bitcoin-mining machines; one customer remains and the line is expected to end by 2026-12-31.

brands.name: CoreWeave license agreements
brands.share: 590 MW leased across five sites, 395 MW billing on 2026-06-30 (120 MW on 2025-12-31); CoreWeave was about 77% of H1 2026 total revenue

brands.name: Data-center portfolio
brands.share: 11 data centers in seven states (AL 1, GA 2, KY 1, NC 1, ND 1, OK 1, TX 4); about 2.1 GW gross utility power, about 1.3 GW leasable customer power (Q2 2026 10-Q)

brands.name: Core Scientific Finance I LLC and its guarantor site subsidiaries (Austin, Denton, Dalton, Marble, Muskogee)
brands.share: Issued $3.3B of 7.750% senior secured notes due 2031 on 2026-05-06, secured by the specified data-center projects

whatsNext.text: Acquisition of Polaris DS LLC (about 40 acres, substation and up to 440 MW of gross power next to Muskogee, OK) for about $421M cash (plus $40M if 40 more MW of firm power arrive before 2026-12-31); $120M held in escrow; expected to close in Q3 2026. No closing filing seen in EDGAR through 2026-09-10, so status after the 10-Q is unconfirmed.
Hosted mining expected to end by 2026-12-31; self-mining wound down
Hunt County, TX campus (431 MW planned) under construction on land bought 2026-05-05 for about $233M

profileAgainst: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (filed 2026-07-28); Form 10-K for the year ended 2025-12-31 (filed 2026-03-02, amended 2026-03-18 only to add an omitted exhibit); 8-Ks through 2026-09-10
